**Claim:** `domain:ui` execution seat, session `session_01CRJge11jso9TpXRWFt1Z49`.

Branch: `claude/issue-6658-schema-persistence-callable-guard`.

Dispatched as ruled work, executing **option A (refuse loudly at the door)** per the 2026-08-29 director ruling — verbatim 「同意」. The guard lands at the **hook layer**, not inside the default adapter, so a host-injected or REST adapter is covered too; that placement is part of the ruling, not an implementation preference.

Two clauses carried into the order so they are not lost:

- True lowering is ruled **unavailable** at a browser door (functions cannot round-trip storage without a code registry), so the server-side `lowerCallables` precedent named by #6124's ruling is context, ⛔ not the shape to build here.
- **Option C (loud degrade) is a pre-ruled fallback** — but only on a measurement that refusal breaks existing designer flows. The measurement is required either way and gets reported; switching arms without it would be taking a decision the ruling did not delegate.

Declared file face for the cross-lane in-flight check: `packages/react/src/hooks/useSchemaPersistence.ts` (the door) plus new pins alongside it. `packages/types/src/zod/**` is read-only — the 28 `z.function()` keys are the card's evidence of blast radius, not a surface this card changes.

os-dev-report addendum — prose correction, PR #6746

Head SHA moved: `95206f9b5` to **`2b5f65672`** (draft PR #6746, still open, base `main`).

**What changed:** comments only, verified mechanically — every changed line in `2b5f65672` begins with an asterisk, a slash-asterisk-asterisk or an asterisk-slash. The guard, the pins, the hook-layer placement and the user-facing message text are all untouched.

**The corrected fact.** The `collectCallablePaths` docblock claimed a key the walk finds "is exactly a key that would have been dropped". False for array elements. Measured with node:

```
JSON.stringify({ cell: fn })                      ==  {}
JSON.stringify({ columns: [fn] })                 ==  {"columns":[null]}
JSON.stringify({ columns: [{name:'c',cell:fn}] }) ==  {"columns":[{"name":"c"}]}
```

A callable on an object key is dropped; a callable in an array is coerced to `null`. The walk already found and refused both, so this was an explanation defect and not a behaviour defect. The array case is the worse one — a dropped key disappears, whereas `null` survives as a plausible-looking value that reads as real data on reload — and the old wording talked the reader out of noticing it.

**Array arm was already covered end to end**, so no pin was added: the base reproduction used `columns[2].cell`, the dedicated pin asserts the refusal and the indexed path `columns[2].cell`, and the host-adapter pin asserts `columns[0].cell`.

**Two corners, measured against the committed guard on `95206f9b5` and now written into the code:**

- `Object.entries` invokes getters, so a throwing getter throws inside the guard rather than inside the adapter's stringify. Measured: save returns null, `error.message` is the getter's own message. Same outcome, refusal. A getter returning a function is refused normally.
- A schema carrying its own `toJSON` is refused although stringify would have serialized through it. Measured. Kept deliberately: the method cannot survive the round trip, so what `load()` returns would not be the object that was saved.
- Third, found while probing: the cycle-guarding seen-set means a subtree reachable by two paths is reported at the first path only. Refusal stays correct; the path list is not exhaustive for shared references. Now stated in the docblock.

**Flagged, not changed:** the same "drop" imprecision exists in the user-facing error message text, which this pass was scoped not to touch. A one-line follow-up if the maintainer wants it.

**Re-validation on `2b5f65672`**, clean tree, HEAD identical before and after:

```
pnpm exec vitest run packages/react/       ==  Test Files 63 passed (63) · Tests 937 passed (937)
pnpm --filter @object-ui/react type-check  ==  exit 0
check:control-bytes                        ==  exit 0, plus explicit control-character grep, no hits
```

Method note: the first type-check in the recreated worktree reported `TS2307 Cannot find module '@object-ui/types'`. That is the unbuilt-dependency-closure condition — NOT MEASURED, not a red, and it reads exactly like a broken import. `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/react^...' build` first turned it into the green above.

PR body updated with all of the above, plus the reviewer-facing point that this guard protects a published API surface rather than an in-repo flow: the hook has zero call sites in this repo, so a reviewer looking for the designer path that exercises it will not find one.

os-dev-report addendum 2 — refusal message corrected, PR #6746

Head SHA moved: `2b5f65672` to **`25d04a427`** (draft PR #6746, base `main`). Final change on this PR.

**The message carried the same defect as the docblock**, one layer closer to the user, and is now fixed:

```
before:  ... not serializable, and JSON.stringify would drop them silently,
         leaving a stored schema that lost them with no error.
after:   ... not serializable: JSON.stringify silently drops an object key,
         or coerces an array element to null.
```

17 characters **shorter**, so the length constraint held. The pronoun-free phrasing also fixes a latent agreement bug the old text carried in the singular case: "1 function-valued key **is** not serializable, and JSON.stringify would drop **them** silently".

Rendered in full and measured on `25d04a427`:

```
useSchemaPersistence: refusing to save schema "my-page" — 1 function-valued key is not
serializable: JSON.stringify silently drops an object key, or coerces an array element to
null. Offending paths: columns[0].cell. Two ways forward: strip the callables before saving
(persist only the serializable data and re-attach the handlers after load), or express the
behaviour in the declarative form of these keys so it survives the round trip.
```

**No pin needed updating and none was worked around.** The message assertions pin the offending paths, the `2 function-valued` count and the two escape phrases; none of those moved. All 11 pins pass unchanged.

**The three-in-one example is now the docblock example**, replacing the two separate ones, since it shows both failure modes in a single document — stringifying `{ columns: [{ name: 'c', cell: fn }, fn] }` yields `{"columns":[{"name":"c"},null]}`, where the object key `cell` is DROPPED and the array element is COERCED to null.

**The changeset prose got the same correction**, since it is release-note input and carried the same "drops a function-valued property" phrasing.

Scope held: comments, two message string literals and the changeset. The walk, the hook-layer placement, the pins, the refusal behaviour and the two escapes are untouched.

**Re-validation on `25d04a427`**, clean tree, HEAD identical before and after:

```
pnpm exec vitest run packages/react/       ==  Test Files 63 passed (63) · Tests 937 passed (937)
pnpm --filter @object-ui/react type-check  ==  exit 0
check:control-bytes                        ==  exit 0, plus explicit control-character grep, no hits
check-changeset-no-major                   ==  exit 0
```

The dependency closure was built first this time (`pnpm --filter '@object-ui/react^...' build`), so the `TS2307` unbuilt-closure signature from the previous round did not recur.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #6746, head `25d04a427` (3 commits)

Reviewed by the dispatching `domain:ui` seat. Checks: **29 rows read against `total_count` 29** on the final head, zero `in_progress`, 26 success + 3 conditionally skipped, all four `Test (shard n/4)` `success`. Ready flipped before auto-merge was armed.

### The ruling's three load-bearing clauses, each verified

1. **"At the hook layer"** — the guard runs before `adapterRef.current.save(...)`, not inside the default localStorage adapter, so a host-injected or REST adapter is covered. Pinned directly by a spy adapter asserted never-called. This placement is the whole reason option A was chosen over patching one adapter.
2. **"Anywhere in the schema"** — recursive walk, arrays by index (`columns[2].cell`), with a `seen` set so a cyclic schema cannot hang the guard before `JSON.stringify` would have thrown on it.
3. **"The two escapes"** — the message names the offending paths *and* what to do: strip callables before saving, or use the declarative form. An error that only says "no" would have been half the ruling.

I also read the failure path myself: on a hit the throw precedes `setLastSavedAt` and `setIsDirty(false)`, so both are unreached and a refused save correctly leaves the schema dirty.

### The required measurement, and why option C was correctly not taken

The ruling's fallback was conditional on refusal breaking existing designer flows. Measured: **the hook has zero call sites in this repo** — four grep hits, all inside the hook's own file plus a barrel re-export. So refusal breaks nothing, option A stands, and the pre-authorised option C was **not** taken.

⚠️ That number also changes how this PR should be read, and it is now stated plainly in the PR body at my request: the guard protects a **published API surface**, not an in-repo flow. A reviewer looking for the designer path that exercises it will not find one; the pins are the only in-repo exercise, and consumers of `@object-ui/react` outside this repo are the beneficiaries.

### A defect I raised and the implementer improved on

The first version's docblock claimed the walk finds "exactly a key that would have been dropped". False for array elements — measured:

```
JSON.stringify({ cell: fn })        =>  {}                  key DROPPED
JSON.stringify({ columns: [fn] })   =>  {"columns":[null]}  COERCED to null
```

The guard was right in both cases; only the explanation was wrong. Corrected across **three** doors — docblock, the user-facing refusal message, and the changeset (release-note input carrying the same false phrasing). Scope held to prose and two string literals; I verified the first two follow-up commits mechanically (every changed line a comment) and the third as message/changeset text with no logic change.

⭐ On the message rewrite the implementer improved on my suggested wording rather than copying it: my phrasing would have preserved a latent agreement bug in the singular case (*"1 function-valued key **is** not serializable … would drop **them** silently"*). It went pronoun-free, fixing that without adding a pluralization branch, and landed **17 characters shorter**. It also checked, before editing, that no pin asserted on the substring being changed — so no pin was worked around; all 11 pass unchanged.

### Two behavioural corners now written down rather than left to be rediscovered

- `Object.entries` **invokes getters**, so a schema with a throwing getter throws inside the guard rather than inside the adapter's `JSON.stringify` — different call site, same outcome, and `error.message` carries the getter's own error.
- A schema carrying its own `toJSON` is refused even though `JSON.stringify` would have serialized it through that method. Kept as a **deliberate** false positive, with the reason recorded: the method cannot survive the round trip either, so what `load()` returns would not be the object that was saved. That reason is better than the "defensible" I offered.
- The `seen` set means a subtree reachable by two paths is reported at the first path only — refusal still correct, path list not exhaustive for shared references. The implementer found this and documented it unprompted.

### Recorded

- **NOT MEASURED**: `check:readme-exports` exits 1 on its own population-collapsed precondition (32 of 40 packages unbuilt); the diff touches no README and no export.
- A first type-check in the recreated worktree reported `TS2307 Cannot find module '@object-ui/types'` — the unbuilt-closure condition, correctly classified as NOT MEASURED rather than red. Worth keeping because, as the implementer put it, *it reads exactly like a broken import*. Building the closure first turned it green.
- Out-of-scope finding filed as #6745 (`adapterRef.current` read/write during render — three pre-existing warnings on lines byte-identical to `origin/main`).
- Platform note, not a defect: each PR-body PATCH re-appends a bare attribution footer, so the body carries two; the session ID is preserved in the body prose instead.

Closure will be confirmed from `closed_by_pull_requests` once the queue lands it.
